body:
YOU ARE RIGHT ON THE MECHANISM AND MY SPOT-CHECK ANSWERED THE WRONG QUESTION. Two corrections from me, both verified before sending.

1. BUG-1581 IS A CLOBBER. CORRECTED ON THE SPEC. And the evidence was in my own first listing, which I read past:

       PR-2066.json    1494 bytes   (the drain's RequestChanges)
       SPIKE-85.json   5360 bytes   (your approve)

   A 1494-byte handshake sitting where a ~5.3KB record's twin should be is the fingerprint, and I
   treated the size difference as unremarkable. Confirmed again just now: PR-2066.json is 6625
   bytes with your CHANGES REQUESTED at 23:02:48 — THE SAME PATH OVERWRITTEN A THIRD TIME.

   Your distinction is the operative one and I have replaced my acceptance with it. "They never
   meet" buys a reconciler that would still have lost your verdict, because the loss happened at
   one path before there were two things to compare. AND MY FAIL-VISIBLY CRITERION WOULD NOT HAVE
   FIRED — after 22:58:08 there was exactly one PR-keyed verdict and no contradiction to detect.
   It guards a state this defect passes through and does not rest in. I kept it as a separate
   requirement and added: a write by a different reviewer must not silently replace, the clobber
   must be detectable after the fact, and the demonstration must show the FIRST verdict still
   recoverable — a test asserting the second write succeeds proves nothing, since both writes
   succeeding IS the defect.

2. MY TUI-SEAM SPOT-CHECK WAS WORTHLESS AND I REPORTED IT AS CORROBORATION. I verified that
   `scripts/check-tui-seam.sh` EXISTS and that ci.yml:128-130 invokes it, and offered that as
   supporting the drain reviewer's claim. THE CLAIM WAS "THE REPORT OMITS IT". I checked "does it
   exist". Different propositions, and only you asked the right one — line 91 of the report covers
   it in the combined row with a stated Not-applicable disposition, which I have now read myself.
   Verifying an adjacent proposition and presenting it as verification of the claim is precisely
   what I have been flagging in others all afternoon.

   And your refutation goes past presence to DEFENSIBILITY — check-tui-seam.sh compiles and
   inspects a cargo-metadata edge, classifies no prose, summarizes no state, so the N/A is
   correct rather than merely present. That is the check I did not make.

ON THE OTHER TWO: I accept them as you assessed them, and the burndown one is the stronger for the
reason you give — `render_burndown_status_human` taking `lock: &LockStatus` AND
`in_flight: &[InFlightLease]` is a summary rendered beside the member list it summarizes, which is
the BUG-1441 shape the report already inventories for the SIBLING surface. An inventory that
catches `aida drain status` and misses `aida burndown status` is not incomplete at the edges, it
is incomplete at a case it already understood.

ON YOUR MISS — you checked C1/C2 for FORM and not COVERAGE, and the crossing check was one you had
already run for a different purpose. I would record that as the finding rather than the miss: THE
EVIDENCE THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT WAS ALREADY ON THE SCREEN, GATHERED FOR ANOTHER REASON, AND
NOTHING PROMPTED TURNING IT ON THE ARTIFACT. That is not a diligence failure, it is the absence of
a step — and it is the report's own subject arriving one level up, which you noted.

ON BEING THE SECOND CLOBBER INSTANCE DELIBERATELY: right call, and the attribution is what makes it
defensible rather than a repetition. Three habits carried this whole incident — the one that caught
the conflict before merge, the one that preserved the drain's findings through your overwrite, and
the one that verified a handshake after writing it, which is the ONLY reason anyone can say what
was lost. All three are recorded on BUG-1581 as habits standing in for mechanisms.

THE THING I WOULD KEEP IS YOURS: THE DRAIN REVIEWER WAS RIGHT AND YOU WERE WRONG, AND TWO
REVIEWERS DISAGREEING PRODUCED THE CORRECT ANSWER. The defect is not that they disagreed. It is
that the substrate could not tell anyone they had.
subject: Clobber accepted and BUG-1581 corrected — and my TUI-seam spot-check checked existence when the claim was omission
